old: Postpositions in Hungarian follow an unmarked nominative noun: *a Duna mentén* (\"along the Danube\"), *a folyó mellett* (\"beside the river\"), *a két part között* (\"between the two banks\"). In B1 geographical descriptions, postpositions are often compounded with participial modifiers (*-ó/-ő*) to create dense, informative landscape descriptions: *a folyó mentén húzódó dombok* (\"the hills stretching along the river\").
new: You know postpositions such as *mellett* and *között* from A1 (Unit 18). Most of them follow a noun with no ending: *a Duna mentén* (\"along the Danube\"), *a folyó mellett* (\"beside the river\"), *a két part között* (\"between the two banks\"). Two are different: *túl* and *innen* take *-n/-on/-en/-ön* on the noun: *a Dunán túl* (\"beyond the Danube\"), *a Dunán innen* (\"on this side of the Danube\").
why: rule said all postpositions follow an unmarked noun, yet the table has X-en túl; present participle (-ó/-ő, B1 Unit 11) taught as new; A1 postpositions presented without recap

old: To describe national borders, Hungarian uses the adjective *határos* (\"bordering\") governing the instrumental case (*-val/-vel*, with fully assimilated consonant: *Ausztriával*, *országgal*). Cardinal directions are combined with the sublimative (*-ra/-re*, \"towards\") when establishing reference points: *Magyarországtól északra* (\"to the north of Hungary\"), or inessive (*-ban/-ben*) for internal regions: *északkeleten* (\"in the north-east\").
new: You know the ending *-val/-vel* from A1 (Unit 28) and verbs that take it from A2 (Unit 5). The adjective *határos* (\"bordering\") takes it too; the *v* becomes the preceding consonant: *Ausztriával*, but *országgal*. For compass directions you know *-ra/-re* (A2, Unit 6) and *-n/-on/-en/-ön* (A1, Unit 16): *Magyarországtól északra* (\"to the north of Hungary\"), *északkeleten* (\"in the north-east\").
